pairs.q: The weight of years of trying and the doubt that you are failing at the one thing that is yours, while the rest of your life asks for everything else.
Doubt and delay feed each other; waiting to feel ready keeps you stuck, and the unacted-on decision weighs more than the work itself.
Your own path walked imperfectly is enough; no honest effort on the right path is ever wasted.
Rise and act; do the work fully and let the result go, one day at a time, and keep at it without waiting to feel ready.
The weight of an exam three weeks away and a mind that won't settle, replaying every rupee your father spent on you.
The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy.
Praise and blame come and go, but what is yours cannot be taken; the effort is yours and the result is not.
Practise steadying the mind for ten minutes before you open the book; let the result go and give the work its full attention.
The feeling of being split between the mother you are and the PM you are, and the ache of a child's question that lands like a verdict.
When duties pull in different directions and fear clouds which one is truly yours, the mind cannot settle; it runs the same loop until one is chosen.
Stay the same in praise and blame; what is yours to do is yours to do, and the result is not in your hands.
Do your own duty without shrinking to fit either picture; give each role its full attention in its own time, and let the rest go.
Being let go after twenty two years in a call that lasted ten minutes, and the hollow morning that follows when the office no longer exists. I lost a parent.
When a result goes wrong, the mind turns against itself; self-blame grows from believing the outcome alone measures our worth, and the harm deepens when we hide it.
A failure is something that happened, not who you are; no one who has served with honesty is ever lost, and no one can take away what you have already built.
Lift yourself up instead of pushing yourself down; learn what this taught you, make amends where you can, and begin again.
The quiet after loss, and the hunger to read something that lasts instead of what passes.
When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass.
What does not pass is the; the texts invite you to read what is real, not what is forwarded.
Reach out to the people and the practice that hold you; seek good company, and remember you are never truly alone.
Being told the life you built will end, and the anger of watching yourself be erased while the one beside you says nothing. Tension with my in-laws.
When others see only a role, their picture shows their smallness; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; they do not decide your worth, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
A fire lit by seeing what others achieved; the resolve to rise, gather your strength and take on what is yours to do.
Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the feeling or looks sideways at the prize; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.
My parents' expectations weigh on me. Being seen as less than you are by the people who ought to know you best, and the anger of watching the life you built get called a phase.
When others see only a role for you, their picture shows their smallness; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit their picture.
The terror of a rating that could end the visa, and the mind that will not stop running until it has checked every message.
Fear grows from imagining the future and from forgetting that what is real in us cannot be lost; worry multiplies what has not happened.
What is real in you cannot be lost, and what is not real is what you are losing sleep over; hold to what is real and let the rest go.
Let go of the result you cannot control, and give your mind one hour of rest a day; when the 2am thought comes, let it pass and return to sleep.
The mind will not settle, caught between the child who no longer needs you and the mother who no longer knows you.
When what we love is passing, the heart aches because the bond was real; grief is love with nowhere to go.
What is real in us cannot be lost; the love that shaped you remains even when the form it wore is gone.
Let the grief have its voice, offer one act of care that is yours alone, and let the rest go.
The real loss of a forty-four-year bond, and the search for what the Gita itself says about where she is now, not what anyone else will tell you.
Grief is love with nowhere to go; everything that comes together must part, and the heart aches because the bond was real, not because it was wrong.
What is real in us cannot be cut or taken; the self is not the body that parts, and that which was yours is not lost.
Read the verses on the self that cannot be cut, burned or dried; sit with them, and let the truth stand without asking it to make the ache smaller.
The pride in their voice and the question at the end of every call, and the restless mind that cannot settle between the two. My parents' expectations weigh on me.
When your worth depends on their approval, every word of blame or pressure shakes you; craving approval keeps the mind unsteady.
Praise and blame come and go like the wind; what is yours to do is yours to do, and no one else can take that from you.
Practise being on your own side; let their praise and their questions come and go without letting either decide your worth today.
Being treated as if your authority is his to give and take, by the man who gave you life, in the place you have built and run for fifteen years. Tension with my in-laws.
When a parent sees only a role instead of a person, their picture shows their smallness; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
Speak the true thing, gently and firmly; hold your ground on what is yours; do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
The shame of being where you are while everyone you know is somewhere else, and the replaying that keeps you from moving.
Comparison and envy burn at another's success; measuring your life against theirs steals the contentment in your own.
What is yours is yours; another's win does not make your path any less real or your effort any less yours.
Measure your own path, not theirs; do one thing that is yours to do today and let the rest go.
A search that began with a book and has become the one company you ask for, the one voice that stays when the house is quiet.
When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass, and the Ramayana is the one thing that does not pass.
What you read in the morning is not a lesson to learn, but a presence to keep; the company you seek is the one that stays when the day is done.
Read the Ramayana as you have been, and let the one verse that speaks to you that day be your only task.
Leaving a life that defined you, and now watching the family you moved for pay the price in the cold and the silence.
When a move is made for someone else's future, the grief for what was left behind grows in the quiet moments; the present pain is real, but it is not the whole cost.
What you chose was real, and so is the grief; the life you built is not the life you lost, and both can be true.
Name what you have given and what you have lost, speak the truth to your family about what this move meant, and hold your ground on the choice you made.
Being treated as less than you are by the people who raised you, and the anger of sitting at your own table and performing normalcy. My parents' expectations weigh on me.
Speak the true thing, gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and find the courage the moment asks for.
The quiet house on the nights the children are not here, and the fear of what your parents will say about it. I'm grieving someone I loved.
Grief is love with nowhere to go, and when it is held back by fear of blame, the mind becomes its own enemy.
What is real in us cannot be lost, and what is lost is not us; the love you feel for your children is your own, and it will not be taken from you.
Let the grief have its place; speak the true thing to one person you trust; and let the quiet house be quiet for a while.
A first win after fourteen months, and the resolve to stay steady through the year ahead instead of riding the wave.
Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the prize; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
Your own path walked imperfectly is enough; no honest effort is ever lost, and effort is yours while results are not.
Rise and act; do your work fully and let the result go, one day at a time.
A mind that has been the provider for eleven years and now cannot settle, with no hour of its own and no answer to what it needs. My parents are getting older far away.
When the mind is never given one quiet minute to rest, it begins to run after results it cannot hold; restlessness grows from a mind that has never been allowed to stop.
The mind that has never been given one quiet minute to rest is not a mind that is broken; it is a mind that has never been allowed to stop.
Give your mind one quiet minute to rest, and let one person know what you need before you decide anything else.
The weight of a promotion you cannot accept, and the replaying of a background that feels like proof you do not belong. I feel like an imposter.
When a result goes wrong, the mind turns against itself; self-blame grows from believing the outcome alone measures our worth, and the more we prove it, the more we need to.
A failure is something that happened, not who you are; no one who tries to do good is ever lost.
Being told your own life is a rich kid's hobby by the man who ought to see you, and the grief of watching your mother cry while he does not look twice.
When a parent sees only a role, their picture shows their smallness; the harm deepens only when their picture starts to replace your own.
What you are cannot be cut smaller by what he sees; he does not decide your worth, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
Speak the true thing to him, gently and firmly; hold your ground on what is yours; do your own duty without shrinking to fit his picture; find the courage the moment asks for.
The shame of snapping at the child you love, and the fear that the face you saw is the face you are becoming.
Anger rises from blocked wanting; it clouds judgement, and a clouded mind says and does what it later regrets.
A clouded mind is not who you are; the calm you bring to your practice is the self that is still there.
Practise seeing the look before it becomes the shout; let the breath come, and speak the true thing gently to your child.
The restless waiting for a son who is not coming back, and the ache of a love that has no place to land.
Grief is love with nowhere to go; the heart aches because the bond was real, and nothing can be done to make the waiting stop.
What is real in us cannot be taken by distance, and the bond that made you a father is not undone by years.
Let the waiting be what it is, and give the love a form it can hold: write him a letter you do not send, or sit with the ache without fighting it.
A mind that will not settle, running on its own, and the phone that keeps it running.
The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy and will not rest.
The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong; holding it feels like holding the wind, but it can be stilled.
Practise steadying the mind through one breath, one task, one moment at a time, and let the phone wait.
The exhaustion of constant care, the shock of being asked who you are by the one you love, and the guilt that follows your own anger. Someone I love is seriously ill.
When a result goes wrong, the mind turns against itself; self-blame grows from believing the outcome alone measures our worth, and grief turns into guilt.
What is real in you cannot be lost; the grief you feel is love with nowhere to go, and it is real, not a failure.
Lift yourself up instead of pushing yourself down; forgive yourself for the human moment, and rest before the next day begins.
Holding everything together for the one you love, and the terror that comes alone am when the search for a number is the only thing left. Someone I love is seriously ill.
What is real in you cannot be lost; your love is not a number you can, and it is what will carry you through.
Do what you can do today for her, and let the rest go; speak your fear to one person you trust, and let the night have its own hour.
The weight of a parent's death after years of silence, and the replaying of a call that was never made.
Grief is love with nowhere to go; the mind turns that love into guilt, and the silence becomes a verdict on a life.
What is real in us cannot be lost; the bond was real, and the love was real, even when the words were not.
Give the love a place to go, make one amend if there is one you can actually make, and let the verdict rest.
A heart that is full of people yet empty, and a search for something deeper than the rituals that have not yet spoken back.
The self you seek is not elsewhere; it is the one that remains when the noise of the house and the ritual fall away.
Sit with the silence after the puja and ask what is asking to be known, not what is owed to be answered.
The ache of a bond that ended too soon, and the loneliness of being the only one who has not let it go. I'm grieving someone I loved.
Grief is love with nowhere to go; the heart aches because what came together was real, and now it has been torn apart.
What was real does not vanish; the bond you shared is still yours, even if the body is not.
Let the grief have its time; speak the name of what you lost, and let the love you have for them find a new place in you.
I'm grieving someone I loved. Inside, my mind won't settle, and I don't know how to carry it.
Grief is love with nowhere to go; the more the bond was real, the deeper the ache when it is taken away, and no one else can give it back.
What is real in us cannot be lost, even when what we loved is taken away; the love remains and so does the ache.
Let the love have its place, speak the true thing about what was lost, and let the grief move without forcing it to be grateful.
Sharing a bed and a life with someone who feels like a colleague, and the loneliness of not knowing when the connection left.
When a bond is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass.
The bond was real, and real things can be found again; you are not alone in feeling the distance, and it is not yours to carry alone.
Living in fear in your own home, hurt by someone who should protect you, and feeling there is no one to turn to.

What is being done to you is not your fault and not your burden to carry; your safety and your worth matter.
Protect yourself and those who depend on you; speak the truth to someone you trust, and find the courage to seek help.
The ache of a love that was real and has now ended, and the mind that will not stop replaying the moment it left.
Grief is love with nowhere to go; everything that comes together must part, and the heart aches because the bond was real.
What is real in you cannot be taken; the love was real, the ending was real, and both can be true at once.
Let the heart feel what it feels, and let the mind rest; do not watch the story again today, and write down what the bond gave you.
The shame of a secret layoff, the daily performance of going to work, and the weight of an EMI that keeps running.

The weight of a failing business and mounting debt, with children's fees due, and the silence of not being able to tell anyone.

What is real in you cannot be taken by what has happened; the effort you made is yours, and no result can take that away.

Praise and blame, success and failure, come and go; what is yours is the effort, not the place on the list.

The shame of an outburst in front of the team, and the knowledge that the anger was not really at the person in front of you.
Praise and blame, honour and disgrace, come and go like the weather; stay the same in the midst of them.
Speak the true thing to the junior, gently and firmly, and name what you were really carrying so it does not sit in the room unseen.
The morning has lost its shape after years in one role, and the question is who you are beyond it.

Sit with the question, read one verse a day, and ask it of yourself without rushing to an answer.
Being treated as if you no longer understand anything, after a lifetime of teaching others to think, and the quiet anger of it. Tension with my in-laws.
Speak the true thing, gently and firmly; hold your ground on what is yours; do your own duty without shrinking to fit their picture.
The fear of pain and of becoming a burden to your children, not the fear of dying itself. I'm afraid of death.

Remember what is real in you and cannot be lost, and let your children hold what they must hold.
Loving the baby and missing the self you were, with the guilt of feeling like a bad mother for both.

Let the grief have its place; speak it to one person who will not judge it, and do one small thing that is just yours before the day begins.

You belong more than you feel right now; the people and the practice that hold you are still within reach.

The form of a practice that once felt alive, and the silence where the feeling used to be.

Return to the practice as if for the first time; let the words carry you past the routine into what they point to.
The wish to hold on to something from your childhood, and to find in the Gita a place to begin.
